   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  October 7th Permanent Memorial ad hoc (Mayor Nazarian and Vice Mayor Mirisch)

 FROM:  Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City Manager

 DATE:  May 13, 2025

 SUBJECT:  Fundraising and Donor Recognition Program

  ATTACHMENT: Dog Park Donor Recognition Flyer

As previously directed by the City Council, staff recommends that the ad hoc initiate a
discussion regarding fundraising and donor recognition for the October 7 th Permanent
Memorial project. As the ad hocs will recall, the City Council has already set aside
$500,000 toward the project, but it is likely that the cost of the memorial may exceed this
amount. As a result, it is important to begin building out the fundraising program. Toward
this end, staff has compiled information about prior fundraising and donor recognition
campaigns.

Beverly Gardens Park
Beverly Gardens Park includes 4 different means of recognizing donors.

  1. The Lily Pond was the first block of Beverly Gardens Park to be renovated. Three
  donations of $200,000 each were made toward restoring this block. Each
  donation/donor is recognized by a plaque on the wall that surrounds the Lily
  Pond.
 2 of 9
   2. The Electric Fountain block was the second block to be renovated. For this block,
  a plaque listing donor names was placed on the wall behind the fountain. The
  donation levels were as follows:
Over $500,000 Largest font size
$200,000-$499,000
$100,000-$199,000
$20,000-$99,000 Smallest font size

  3 of 9
 3. The remaining blocks of Beverly Gardens Park were renovated as a group. Two
  large donations were received as part of this phase of the construction. One was
  for $750,000. In recognition for this donation, plaques were placed on boulders at
  either side of the Cactus Garden. Another donation was received for $1 million.
  In recognition for this donation, 2 plaques were placed on 2 boulders, and each
  boulder was placed in each of two of the smaller blocks of Beverly Gardens Park.

  4 of 9
 The fourth methodology of donor recognition is the adopt a bench program which will be
addressed below.

Dog Park
The Beverly Hills Dog Park included three different ways of donor recognition.
  1. The first is a donor wall which includes plaques of differing sizes, based on the
  amount of the donation. The attached flyer lists the sizes and amounts
  associated with each type of plaque.

  5 of 9
   2. The second means of recognition was for the donation of two mature oak trees.
  These trees were valued at approximately $40,000 each. Each tree has a plaque
  and pedestal at the base.
  The third method of donor recognition is with the bench adoption program, which is
  described below.

Adopt a Bench Program
The adopt a bench program allows for donors to select certain benches in particular City
parks on which a dedication plaque can be placed. Each bench that is available to be
adopted has an insert where the plaque can be mounted. For the benches that are
available through this program, donors may adopt a bench for $5000. In all locations,
except for the dog park, the donor plaque remains in place for 10 years. In the dog park,
the bench plaques are to remain in perpetuity.

  6 of 9
 9/11 Memorial
Fundraising was also conducted for the 9/11 memorial in front of the Beverly Hills Fire
Department. As part of this program, different levels of donors were established, such as
Partners, Benefactors, Guardians, Patrons, etc. The funding for each of these levels will
be shared at the ad hoc meeting. Donor names are carved in a stone plaque.

  7 of 9
 Additionally, there is a separate stone monument which lists the names of individuals or
companies that dedicated substantial in-kind donations to the project.

  8 of 9
 While the responses to the Request for Proposals are not due until May 16th, staff believes
that it can be assumed that the site for the October 7 th memorial will have a wall or
monument on which donors can be recognized. As the ad hoc will recall, the Council
indicated that all donor recognition should occur on the perimeter of the memorial, and
not as part of the memorial itself. Since it will still be some months before the final design
of the memorial is selected, staff feels that it is prudent to begin the discussion about
fundraising/donor recognition early. As a result, it is recommended that the October 7 th
Ad Hoc members discuss previous fundraising activities and initiate a discussion
regarding the development of a fundraising/donor recognition program for the October 7 th
memorial. Once the fundraising program is established by the ad hoc, it will be shared
with the Beverly Hills Community Charitable Foundation which will work on the goal of
raising the funds.

  9 of 9
   Beverly Hills
  Community Dog Park
  Donor Recognition
All donors will be recognized in the Community Services’
quarterly brochure, the dog park opening day program,
and online on the Dog Park page of the City’s website.

Donations at these levels will be recognized with a perma-
nent plaque placed on the interior wall of the dog park.

  Donation Amount  Plaque Size
  $1,000  2 inches x 10 inches
  $5,000  2 ½ inches x 11 inches
  $10,000  3 inches x 12 inches
  $25,000  4 inches x 14 inches
  $50,000  5 inches x 18 inches
  $100,000+  7 inches x 28 inches

  For more information please visit
  www.beverlyhills.org/dogpark or call 310-285-2531
